newsitem.title: CANADA: Gibraltar plans US$140 mln debt offer.
newsitem.headline: Gibraltar plans US$140 mln debt offer.

text.p: Gibraltar Mines Ltd said Thursday it received a commitment from underwriters for a US$140 million debt offering to back development of its delayed Lomas Bayas copper project in Chile.
Gibraltar said in July it was unable to secure an underwriting commitment for US$160 million in debt and announced a delay in development.

Gibraltar said Thursday it is seeking the balance of the funding necessary to begin development of the project but did not specify an amount. "Our intent continues to be to develop Lomas Bayas in the earliest possible timeframe and start-up of the plant should occur in 1998," it said.

Lomas Bayas is slated to be an open pit mine and processing plant with capacity for 60,000 tonnes of copper cathode a year. Gibraltar previously said the total cash requirements for the project were US$240 million including debt of US$185 million.
BZW Mining Finance is lead arranger for the debt offer.
Barclays Bank Plc will underwrite US$70 million, Dresdner Bank Canada US$50 million and a Dresdner affiliate, Deutsch Sudamerikanische Bank AG, US$20 million.
The underwriting agreement requires finalization of documentation by the end of the year.
Total mineable reserves at Lomas Bayas are 2.277 billion pounds of copper at a grade of 0.36 percent.

Gibraltar blamed a sharp fall in copper prices in July for the delay. It said Thursday the debt commitment in current copper market conditions "provides independent confirmation of the strong economics of the Lomas Bayas project."
